| [NOTE-050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-050.md) v2 | The relativity of causal knowledge | The paper defines SCMs as functors I → Prob and interventions as natural transformations (which requires invertible mixing functions). It encodes each non-intervened SCM as the convex space Δ(V, Ω) of all probability measures on its endogenous space, and puts these spaces on a graph as stalks of a network sheaf and cosheaf. The restriction maps are interventionally consistent α-abstractions and the extension maps are unspecified affine maps. "Relative causal knowledge" is the image of alternating restriction and extension along a path (Def. 11). The two substantive-looking theorems are either unsound or vacuous. Theorem 1 (every convex combination of a model's interventional measures is a soft-interventional measure of it) rests on a proof step that is false. Theorems 2 and 3 hold for any pushforward map, so interventional consistency does no work in them. There are no results about the sheaf. | Read |

| [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md) v2 | Pernu — Mental causation via neuroprosthetics? | The interventionist/difference-making case for nonreductive mental causation from BCIs (List & Menzies 2009; Menzies 2015; Woodward 2008a,b, 2017) misplaces multiple realisation. What the ensemble recordings show is that one cortical-level variable N (the ensemble's average firing) is realised by many single-neuron patterns N1, N2. Each intention M corresponds to one value of N. So the counterfactual contrast "∼M □→ ∼B true, ∼N □→ ∼B false" fails, and neuroprosthetics supports mental causation only by identifying M with N, not nonreductive physicalism. | Read |
| [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md) v2 | Quillien — Luck and intentional action | Across three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; Likert 1–7), judgments that "X happened because the agent wanted X" track intentionality judgments under manipulations of luck. | [NOTE-111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-111.md) v2 | Baedke et al. — Unknotting reciprocal causation | The paper gives an epistemic, not a metaphysical, tool for organism–environment reciprocal causation. | [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md) v2 | Poltorak — Wave-function realism and causal closure | A closure principle has two tacit parameters, its domain and its completeness relation (causal, dynamical or explanatory). The physicalist is left with a dilemma: STC is too narrow, and FPC needs an independent criterion of physicality plus a dynamical-to-causal bridge. The paper tests this across primitive-ontology, spacetime-state, multi-field, Everettian, nomological and dispositional readings. | Read |
| [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md) v2 | Hazelwood — Emerging dilemma for reciprocal causation | Hazelwood defines RC as "the process of natural selection is both a cause and effect of processes such as niche construction" and EC as "natural selection is an emergent causal process". He argues they are incompatible. Emergence here is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as Pence's composition. If EC holds, niche construction partly composes selection, so the two fail Woodward's independent-fixability condition and cannot stand in a causal relation. If EC fails, selection is either non-causal (statisticalism) or individual-level, which is incoherent because relative fitness needs a population (Millstein, Sober). EES proponents should drop RC but can keep niche construction as a genuine cause of the evolutionary *product*. | Read |
| [NOTE-585](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-585.md) | Causation and Manipulability | A survey of manipulability theories that states Woodward's own. X causes Y iff some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is a surgical, exogenous cause of X meeting conditions M1–M4. The account is non-reductive but not viciously circular, needs no human agent, and defines total, direct and contributing causes by combinations of interventions. Invariance and higher-level causation are not discussed. | Read |
